author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Voting began Sunday in Sweden’s parliamentary election after opinion polls showed a close contest between Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson’s governing right-wing bloc and the centre-left opposition led by Social Democrat Magdalena Andersson. Polls were scheduled to open at 8 a.m. local time and close at 8 p.m., with exit polling expected after voting ends.

Kristersson has said the Sweden Democrats would enter a four-party government for the first time if the right wins. The party has supported his minority administration in parliament during the past four years. The centre-left entered election day with a narrow polling lead, but the gap tightened late in the campaign.

The result may turn partly on whether the Liberals clear the 4% threshold required to win parliamentary seats. Both blocs support Ukraine and higher military spending, but differ over welfare spending, taxes, immigration and nuclear power. Coalition talks could be complicated regardless of which side wins the most support, making the count and party thresholds central to the developing outcome.
dek: Voters are choosing between the governing right-wing bloc and a narrowly leading centre-left opposition.
headline: Sweden begins close parliamentary election with government at stake
